title: Every live check against the production model
request: With the owner's yes and a cap, run every live check on the production model: every model path, the five fixed specialist cases and the judgment suite, on synthetic or public data only. Report per path and case what the model proposed and what the code accepted or refused, with requests, tokens and euros; keep every failure in the record; fix defects with a scripted-client test. The owner added credit and asked to keep usage small without removing or reducing the model calls the product makes.
spec: make model-paths ARGS='--configured --cap-eur 2', the five specialist cases, make agent-eval-live ARGS='--yes --cap-eur 2'; each with requests, tokens and euros; every provider or executor failure stays in the result; anything that broke gets a fix and a test.
plan: Check that the key reaches the platform and which models it may use (a free model listing), switch the configured model to gpt-6-luna, and set its price so the euro caps can stop spending.
Run the judgment suite live with a small cap: it failed on its first request (kept as AEV-012).
Send one tiny tool-calling request shaped like DCLab's to read the provider's actual error.
Fix the client so it learns the model's tool rule from the refusal; fix the specialists' start-up in the agent environment; test both with scripted clients.
Rerun with caps: the model paths, the five specialist cases, and the judgment suite with two repeats (AEV-013).
Review with 14.3; fix the findings; make check-all; commit.

decisions.decision: The failed live run stays as its own result (AEV-012); the rerun is a new result.
decisions.why: The package requires every provider failure to stay in the record, never replaced by a mock or a later success.

decisions.decision: The client learns from the refusal and retries once with reasoning_effort 'none', then sends it from the start for that model.
decisions.why: The provider refuses function tools on chat completions for this model unless reasoning is off; a fixed per-model table would go stale, and one retry costs nothing because a refused request is not billed.

decisions.decision: Live results say their scores are for the model without reasoning on tool turns.
decisions.why: Otherwise results labelled with the model's name would be compared later as if reasoning had been on.

decisions.decision: The model's price was entered in euros at its dollar figure.
decisions.why: While the euro is worth more than the dollar this overstates spend, the safe direction for caps.

change: models/client.py: on a refusal naming reasoning_effort and 'none' while tools are present, remember the model and retry once with reasoning_effort 'none' (complete and stream); the refused attempt counts in the usage log and the result states the effort. storage/url.py: the database switch is read without SQLAlchemy so the agent environment can open the gateway. agent_eval/live.py loads .env before importing the gateway. A price for gpt-6-luna. Results AEV-012, AEV-013 and the specialists' file.

findings.defect: The first live run failed every tool request.
findings.scenario: The judgment suite on gpt-6-luna stopped after one request with 'the model request failed'; a direct tiny request showed the provider's 400: function tools with reasoning_effort are not supported for this model on chat completions; use the Responses API or set reasoning_effort to 'none'.
findings.cause: The model refuses function tools on chat completions unless reasoning is off.
findings.fix: The client learns that from the refusal, retries once with reasoning_effort 'none' and sends it from the start afterwards.

findings.defect: The specialist cases could not start in the agent environment.
findings.scenario: In .venv-agent the usage log imported SQLAlchemy through the storage module although no database was configured, and that environment has no SQLAlchemy.
findings.cause: The database switch was read through a module that imports SQLAlchemy.
findings.fix: A small storage/url.py reads the switch without SQLAlchemy; routing, shadow and usage use it.
findings.test: AgentEnvironmentTests: the gateway opens on files with SQLAlchemy blocked.

findings.defect: The live suite's plan showed the old model and no model available.
findings.scenario: Running the live suite printed a plan naming the previous model, as if .env were not read.
findings.cause: The live suite did not load .env when no gateway was given.
findings.fix: live.py loads .env when no gateway is given.

findings.defect: The retry was invisible to the usage log, and results did not say reasoning was off.
findings.scenario: The gateway recorded one attempt with outcome ok for two HTTP requests; the refusal was never written; request caps undercount by one per model per process; results labelled 'gpt-6-luna' were really 'gpt-6-luna without reasoning on tool turns', which matters for 14.5's comparisons.
findings.cause: The retry happened inside the client, below the gateway's accounting.
findings.fix: The refused request counts as an attempt in the usage log, and a live result states its scores are without reasoning on tool turns.

findings.defect: Two .env settings were ignored by the live suite.
findings.scenario: The gateway reads DCLAB_MODEL_RETRIES and DCLAB_MODEL_BACKOFF at import, and live.py imported it before loading .env, so values set there were not used.

findings.defect: Only the happy path of the retry was tested.
findings.scenario: No test that a different 400 is raised once and not retried, that a refused retry surfaces as one error, or that the model is not added to the remembered set on an unrelated error.
findings.fix: A scripted create that raises an unrelated error: one request sent, the error raised, the model not remembered.

measurements.name: model paths on gpt-6-luna
measurements.gate: Each path runs on the production model with a cap; every failure stays in the result.
measurements.result: All five paths ran: 21 requests, none failed, about €0.005 (synthetic design, log pattern at parse rate 1.0, the Home chat with a 10-node workflow the check accepted, cited evidence with an honest 'not covered', the intern's five tools).

measurements.name: five specialist cases
measurements.gate: Each fixed case passes its hard checks.
measurements.result: All five passed, one request each.

measurements.name: judgment suite live, two repeats (AEV-013)
measurements.gate: Run with a cap and report each score with its interval; no pass threshold was set for this run.
measurements.result: Leaks caught 0.96 (95%: 0.47–1.0), false alarms 0.28 (0–0.59), valid moves and citations 1.0; 547 requests, 3.25 M input and 31 k output tokens.
measurements.next: Nearly every intern run ended on its step budget rather than finishing, and input tokens dominate the cost; two repeats are too few for tight intervals.

outcome: Done (7f2a256, about €0.35 in all): every live check ran on gpt-6-luna after two fixes found by running them; the failed first run is kept as AEV-012. Open: the intern's runs end on the step budget; input tokens dominate cost; two repeats give wide intervals; scores are for the model without reasoning on tool turns.
lessons: Keep the failed live run as evidence and rerun into a new result; a later success never replaces it.
When a provider refuses a request, send one minimal request yourself to read the real error before changing code.
A retry below the accounting layer makes usage and caps lie; count every attempt where the money is counted.
A score must name the configuration it was measured under, here reasoning off on tool turns.
